Screenshots included; no evidence of attached STK software files
Report structure (Exec Summary, Introduction, Mission Design, Conclusion, Bibliography)

technical_issues.issue: "A very high altitude would yield low resolution images which is also desirable" – should read 'undesirable'; contradicts design logic.

"significant J2 perturbations as a result of its highly polar inclination" is imprecise: RAAN precession ∝ cos(i) is zero at i=90°; SSO relies on retrograde inclination (~98°), not polar proximity per se.

Graveyard-orbit discussion is largely irrelevant for a LEO satellite; EOL paragraph is redundant/contradictory ("without thrusters... uncontrolled descent... However, the ZYZZsat is without thrust capability").
Drag-sail sentence is incomplete: "utilising a large surface area to ‘ and is suitable".
Wikipedia used as a source, explicitly disallowed; references lack titles, authors and access dates.
Access table numbering is inconsistent (first row unnumbered, duplicate access 14/15) – possibly an OCR artefact but should be checked.

overall: A well-structured, technically sound preliminary mission design addressing all space-segment requirements with genuine STK evidence and hand calculations. Weakened by missing software files, unnumbered figures/tables, bare-URL references including Wikipedia, and several technical/editorial slips. Weighted score ≈ 7.3/10.

feedback.summary: You produced a well-structured, technically sound preliminary mission design for ZYZZsat, addressing all space-segment requirements with genuine STK evidence and hand calculations. Your introduction, launch/orbit/ground-control rationale and conclusions are strong. To reach the top rubric levels, attach your STK software files, add numbered figure/table captions, replace Wikipedia and bare-URL references with proper citations, and fix the technical and editorial slips noted below.
next_steps: Attach your STK scenario files (or export packages) in an appendix so your access and orbit results can be verified, and number all figures and tables (e.g. Figure 1, Table 1) with captions referenced in the text.
Replace the Wikipedia citation and bare URLs with full references (authors, titles, year, access dates) in a consistent style, and ensure every in-text citation matches the reference list.

Proofread carefully: correct 'undesirable' in the orbit altitude discussion, complete the broken drag-sail sentence, rewrite the contradictory EOL/graveyard-orbit paragraph for your LEO satellite, and fix the J2/RAAN explanation (precession ∝ cos i, zero at i = 90°; SSO uses ~98° retrograde inclination).
